title: 树梢挂金灯  (Stringing Gold Above the Tree)

segments.t: At eleven o'clock, Peng joins Hao on the upper balcony to pass braided lantern cord down toward the courtyard tree, while Mei stands beside the stone basin below shielding her eyes and calling directions. Let us listen in first.
老弟，左边那根绳子慢点儿——你那边再抬高十厘米左右！
你们俩就停在那儿！从厨房门口看过去，那道弧线美极了！
每条绳子上能夹几盏纸灯笼，才不会把绳子压弯？
每条挂六个圆灯笼，算下来桌子上方一共有二十四轮亮月亮！
暖金色和浅珊瑚色错开挂，整个石板院子就像晚霞一样！
小美，在下面树枝那儿接住第三条绳子的绳头！
稳稳接住了！快告诉我打哪种结，才能一直绷紧到明晚？
在铁环上绕两圈再拉个双套结——这是爷爷教咱俩的！
你看树梢的叶子沙沙响，起风了。
刚才从街口拱门吹过来的那阵凉风，你们感觉到了吗？
那些娇气的纸灯球，要不要先试试下午的风再撑开？
来不及了——周经理已经把第一条绳上的十二盏都撑开了，正大步往外走呢！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
老弟，左边那根绳子慢点儿——你那边再抬高十厘米左右！

'Easy on the left cord, little brother—raise your side about ten centimeters higher!' Older brother Peng calls Hao "laodi" ("little brother") and pairs "tai gao" ("lift high") with "zuoyou" ("about" or "give or take").
你们俩就停在那儿！从厨房门口看过去，那道弧线美极了！

'Hold it right there, both of you! From the kitchen door, that curve looks magical!' Adding "jile" ("to the extreme") after "mei" ("beautiful") turns "mei jile" into an enthusiastic "gorgeous beyond words."
每条绳子上能夹几盏纸灯笼，才不会把绳子压弯？

'How many paper lanterns can we clip along each line without weighing the cord down?' A lantern takes the dedicated counter "zhan" ("ji zhan zhi denglong"), and "ya wan" describes heavy weight bending the cord down.
每条挂六个圆灯笼，算下来桌子上方一共有二十四轮亮月亮！
'Six round lanterns per line makes twenty-four glowing moons above the tables!' "Suan xialai" means "adding it all up," while poetic "lun" counts full glowing moons ("ershisi lun liang yueliang").
暖金色和浅珊瑚色错开挂，整个石板院子就像晚霞一样！

'Alternate warm gold and soft coral so the whole stone courtyard feels like sunset!' "Cuokai gua" means to stagger or alternate as you hang things, and "jiu xiang ... yiyang" compares the glow to evening clouds ("wanxia").
小美，在下面树枝那儿接住第三条绳子的绳头！
'Catch the end of line three down by the lower tree branch, Mei!' Hao attaches "zhu" to "jie" ("catch") in "jiezhu" to guarantee a firm catch, while "shengtou" literally names the cord end.
稳稳接住了！快告诉我打哪种结，才能一直绷紧到明晚？

'Caught cleanly! Tell me what kind of knot keeps this cord tight until tomorrow evening!' "Da jie" is "to tie a knot" ("da na zhong jie" asks "which kind of knot"), and "bengjin" means stretched good and tight.
在铁环上绕两圈再拉个双套结——这是爷爷教咱俩的！

'Wrap twice around the iron ring and pull a double hitch—Grandfather taught us both!' Counting loops uses "quan" ("rao liang quan", wrap two circles), and inclusive "zanlia" warmly brings speaker and listener together as "us two."
你看树梢的叶子沙沙响，起风了。

'Look at the leaves rustling at the top of the tree; the breeze is picking up.' Hao uses "shasha" to mimic dry leaves brushing together, and compact "qi feng le" announces that a breeze has started up.
刚才从街口拱门吹过来的那阵凉风，你们感觉到了吗？
'Did you feel that cool gust blowing through the street arch just now?' "Zhen" measures a sudden burst of wind ("na zhen liangfeng"), while "gangcai" points to just a moment ago.
那些娇气的纸灯球，要不要先试试下午的风再撑开？

'Should we test the afternoon wind first before unfolding those delicate paper globes?' "Jiaoqi" playfully treats the fragile paper lanterns like something easily bruised, and "chengkai" means to pop them open.
来不及了——周经理已经把第一条绳上的十二盏都撑开了，正大步往外走呢！

'Too late—Zhou already opened twelve lanterns on line one, and he's marching right out!' "Lai bu ji le" means "there's no time left," while "zheng ... ne" catches Zhou mid-stride ("dabu wang wai zou") right now.
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.
老弟，左边那根绳子慢点儿——你那边再抬高十厘米左右！
你们俩就停在那儿！从厨房门口看过去，那道弧线美极了！

暖金色和浅珊瑚色错开挂，整个石板院子就像晚霞一样！
小美，在下面树枝那儿接住第三条绳子的绳头！

在铁环上绕两圈再拉个双套结——这是爷爷教咱俩的！
你看树梢的叶子沙沙响，起风了。
刚才从街口拱门吹过来的那阵凉风，你们感觉到了吗？
那些娇气的纸灯球，要不要先试试下午的风再撑开？
来不及了——周经理已经把第一条绳上的十二盏都撑开了，正大步往外走呢！
Twenty-four lantern hooks span the sky above the courtyard, right as the afternoon breeze picks up speed! See you next time.
下次见！
